cohort: The study included 980 pregnant women diagnosed with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) at a tertiary care referral center between 2012 and 2021.
finding: The study found that HDP cases had an increased risk of abruptio placenta, PPH, fetal growth restriction, prematurity, and a significantly higher cesarean delivery rate.
mod_finding: Patients with HDP had a significantly higher cesarean delivery rate (61.64%).
